advisory.checklist_item: - [ ] Reconcile the `--` escape-hatch claim in `_wants_help`'s docstring/comment with the fact that value-taking handlers (e.g. create_cli) do not honor `--` as an argument terminator.
evidence: src/rebar/_cli/__init__.py:135: "``--`` ends option scanning so a caller can still pass a literal ``--help`` token as data after it."
composer.py:368-373: `elif a.startswith("-"): ... print(f"Error: unrecognised option '{a}'\n{_USAGE}") ; return 2` — `--` is not stripped/handled as a terminator by create_cli
ABSENCE: no `--` argument-terminator handling exists in composer.create_cli's option loop (composer.py:325-376)
advisory.finding: The `_wants_help` docstring and the dispatcher comment assert that `--` lets a caller 'pass a literal --help token as data after it', but value-taking write handlers such as create_cli do not treat `--` as an argument terminator — `rebar create task -- --help` hits the 'unrecognised option' error path (composer.py:368-373) rather than storing `--help` as data, so the documented escape hatch is misleading for those commands.
scenarios: User runs `rebar create task -- --help` expecting a ticket titled `--help` per the documented escape hatch

advisory.checklist_item: - [ ] Confirm intercepting `--help`/`-h` in value-position of value-taking options (e.g. create's -p/-d/--assignee) is acceptable, or scope the scan to skip option-value tokens.
evidence: src/rebar/_cli/__init__.py:129-143: `_wants_help` returns True on ANY `--help`/`-h` before `--`, regardless of whether the preceding token is a value-consuming option
composer.py:349-356: `elif a in ("--priority", "-p") and i + 1 < n: priority = args[i + 1]` — the next token is consumed as an arbitrary value, which could legitimately be `--help`
advisory.finding: A `--help`/`-h` intended as the VALUE of a value-taking option is now intercepted as a help request. create_cli accepts arbitrary string values for -p/--priority, -d/--description, --assignee, --tags, etc.; previously `rebar create task title -p --help` passed `--help` as the priority value, but the any-position scan now short-circuits to usage, making such values unreachable via the CLI.
scenarios: `rebar create task title --description --help` (or any option whose value is literally `--help`/`-h`)

advisory.checklist_item: - [ ] Add a test that `rebar create task -- --help` treats `--help` as a literal title, performs a CREATE write (ticket count +1), and exits 0 (covers the `--` terminator branch of `_wants_help`).
evidence: src/rebar/_cli/__init__.py:138-143 `for tok in rest: if tok == "--": return False` — the terminator branch under review

Docstring at src/rebar/_cli/__init__.py:135 `"--" ends option scanning so a caller can still pass a literal --help token as data after it` and test-file docstring `"--" remains the escape hatch` — behavior is a claimed contract
src/rebar/_commands/__init__.py:103-105 confirms tokens after `--` are literal positionals, so `create task -- --help` is an observable write (ticket titled --help, exit 0)
ABSENCE: no parametrize case or test in test_create_help_no_write_b8de.py includes a `--` token; regression in the terminator branch would go undetected
advisory.finding: The `--` terminator escape-hatch branch of `_wants_help` (a `--help`/`-h` token appearing AFTER a `--` must be treated as literal data, not a help request) is documented as part of the repaired contract but has no test. The suite would stay green if the `if tok == "--": return False` line were removed or broken.
scenarios: `rebar create task -- --help` should create a ticket whose title is the literal `--help` and exit 0; a break in the terminator branch would instead print usage and write nothing
